summary: OpalMetrics: request-priority inversion → failover cascade causing streaming SLO breaches and invoice variance
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC OpalMetrics reported persistent streaming disconnects and slow tail latencies for high-priority scoring calls. Initial symptoms looked like throttling and 5xx errors but investigation found systemic priority inversion in request routing followed by failover amplification to a quantized model variant. Impact: sustained SLO breaches for conversational streaming endpoints, duplicated completions for long-running batch requests, and a downstream invoice variance for OpalMetrics. This ticket captures timeline, triage notes, mitigation, and follow-up actions.
impact: OpalMetrics production traffic (enterprise plan) experienced ~18% request error rate for streaming endpoints and 2.3x tail latency on p99 for 30 minutes. Customer reported missing events in downstream scoring pipelines and a projected billing overage due to duplicate requests. SLA window flagged — customer escalated to CS and assigned P0.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send mixed-priority traffic: interleave streaming/high-priority scoring requests with large low-priority batch embeddings for the same tenant (simulate 1:3 ratio).
2) Observe request routing: per-worker queues saturate causing high-priority requests to be queued behind long-running low-priority tasks.
3) Trigger failover by simulating a small GPU pool pressure so autoscaler marks pool degraded; observe fallback policy routing to quantized variant and duplicate-invocation amplification.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: throttling at ingress layer due to per-tenant token rate limit — disproved by rate-limit metrics (no wild spikes).

Heap of evidence pointed to per-worker FIFO queues and lack of preemption: long-running low-priority batch tasks were occupying workers and preventing high-priority streaming requests from being scheduled (priority inversion).

Failover policy design: when node pool reported degraded capacity, router triggered immediate failover to a compatible quantized variant but also retried requests without de-duplicating in-flight requests, causing duplicate completions and billing anomalies.

Observed autoscaler behavior: a rapid short-lived GPU availability drop (OOM on one replica during a heavy background maintenance job) caused scheduler to mark pool degraded; autoscaler later recovered within ~2m but failover amplification window had already started.
comments: Lina Park (Support): 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC — Received first customer report; opened P0 and paged SRE. Customer seeing streaming disconnects on live scoring path.
Ravi Menon (SRE): 2026-03-10 14:34 UTC — Identified long queues on worker gd-11; suspected per-worker FIFO queueing. Kicked off targeted routing rule to drain batch tasks for opalmetrics tenant.

Evan Chen (Eng - Serving Runtime): 2026-03-10 15:02 UTC — Confirmed failover codebase triggers immediate retry to fallback without checking dedupe header. Preparing hotfix to gate duplicate resends behind idempotency token.
OpalMetrics (Customer): 2026-03-10 15:45 UTC — Customer acceptance of temporary throttling workaround; requested written action plan for billing variance and mitigation to prevent recurrence.
Ravi Menon (SRE): 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC — Patch deployed (PR#4821). Added per-tenant preemption threshold and dedupe check for failover retries; monitoring green for 24h.
resolution: Mitigation: 1) Emergency routing rule applied to prioritize high-priority streaming requests for tenant opalmetrics and to preempt long-running low-priority tasks. 2) Temporary quota increase provided to OpalMetrics while the pool stabilized. 3) Hotfix (PR#4821) deployed to serving-runtime to add idempotency guard for failover retries and to introduce a preemption-aware scheduling policy. Root cause: combined effect of per-worker FIFO queues (no preemption) and failover retry logic that resubmitted in-flight requests without deduplication when pool health flapped. Result: resolved duplicate invocations, tail latency restored to baseline, and streaming disconnects ceased.
postincident_actions: 1) Engineering to refactor router scheduling: implement priority-aware worker preemption and bounded preemption cost model (owner: SRE/serving-runtime; ETA: 2026-04-15).
2) Deploy improved health gating for failover: require idempotency token or explicit dedupe header before resending in-flight requests (owner: Serving Runtime; completed 2026-03-11).
3) Update runbook and add a new play for mixed-priority traffic tenants to proactively set preemption thresholds (owner: Support; ETA: 2026-03-18).
4) Issue a customer-facing invoice reconciliation and apply credit for duplicate-invocation billing exposure (owner: Finance/CS; ETA: 2026-03-16).
5) Create a detection alert for 'priority inversion' signature: sustained high queue depth + increased p99 for high-priority requests (owner: Observability; ETA: 2026-03-20).
